images.name: duties
images.title: Legal intake, *duty by duty*
rows: Answers calls, forms and chats within a minute and routes existing clients to their lawyer's team.
Asks the firm's questions for each practice area and writes up the answers.
Collects the names and searches the practice management system. A person clears any match.
Books the right lawyer under the firm's rules and sends the intake form.
Reschedules no-shows and reminds people about unsigned engagement letters.
Gives no opinion on the merits. Passes the matter to a lawyer with a summary.

images.name: evening
images.title: An evening of *legal intake*
rows: A web form asks about a will for a couple with two children. It screens and books a video consultation.
Reminds a client that the engagement letter sent Friday is still unsigned.
A caller was rear-ended on the way home. It screens, runs the conflict search and books a consultation.
A caller has a custody hearing on Friday. It flags the intake as urgent for a family lawyer.
A conflict search finds the opposing party's company in the system. It sends it to the person who clears conflicts.
A caller describes threats from a former partner. It gives the firm's safety instructions and alerts a lawyer.
Answers a question about parking and what to bring to tomorrow's consultation.

images.name: setup
images.title: How AI legal intake *is set up*
steps: Read your bar's AI guidance and settle vendor terms before any client data.
Pull a month of inquiries and write screening questions for each practice area.
Contacts, conflict search and calendar. No open case files.
Advice, conflicts, fees, deadlines and safety risks go to a named person.
It drafts intake summaries while a lawyer reads each one, then takes on more.
Update it when practice areas, fees or lawyers change.
